title: Billing Rules for Claims Invoices and Administrative Invoices under the PBM Services Agreement
content:
Northbridge Rx bills a plan sponsor under its PBM Services Agreement on two kinds of invoice: claims invoices for drug cost, and monthly administrative invoices for per-employee fees. The billing basis for claims follows the pricing model of the sponsor's pricing arrangement.

## 1. Billing basis for claims, by pricing model

1.1 **Spread.** Claims are billed at the guaranteed rates of the arrangement (the guaranteed discounts off average wholesale price for brand retail, generic retail, brand home delivery, generic home delivery and specialty claims), plus the retail dispensing fee or the home delivery dispensing fee, whatever the pharmacy was paid.

1.2 **Pass-through.** Claims are billed at exactly what the pharmacy was paid. The same guaranteed rates are guaranteed in aggregate, and any shortfall against them is credited at the annual reconciliation.

1.3 **Cost-plus.** Claims are billed at acquisition cost multiplied by one plus the cost-plus markup, plus the dispensing fee.

1.4 The member cost share collected by the pharmacy is never billed to the sponsor.

| Pricing arrangement | Pricing model that sets the claims billing basis |
|---|---|
| Northbridge Traditional Pricing | spread |
| Northbridge Pass-Through Pricing | pass-through |
| Northbridge Transparent Cost-Plus | cost-plus |
| Northbridge Rebate Guarantee Plus | pass-through |
| Northbridge Enterprise Value | pass-through |
| Northbridge Coalition Purchasing | pass-through |

## 2. Invoices and periods

2.1 Each claims invoice covers one period of the arrangement's claims invoicing cycle.

2.2 The administrative invoice for a month is the administrative fee per employee per month plus the clinical program fee per employee per month, that sum multiplied by the employee-months enrolled. Both fees are the figures of the sponsor's own pricing arrangement.

2.3 A claims period or fee month is invoiced only once: a claims period appears on one claims invoice, and a fee month on one administrative invoice, for the same agreement. A claims invoice and an administrative invoice are different invoices and do not duplicate each other even when their periods begin on the same day.

## 3. Market checks

Market checks of the pricing guarantees run every number of months set by the arrangement's market check interval, when that interval is not zero; with an interval of zero no market check runs.

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs only)

**Administrative invoice.** Hypothetical fees of 3.00 (administrative) and 0.40 (clinical program) per employee per month, and 1200 employee-months enrolled in the month: 3.00 plus 0.40 gives 3.40; 3.40 multiplied by 1200 gives an administrative invoice of 4080.00 USD.

**Cost-plus claim.** Hypothetical acquisition cost 50.00, markup 10% and dispensing fee 2.00: 50.00 multiplied by 1.10 gives 55.00; adding the dispensing fee gives 57.00 billed to the sponsor. Any cost share the member paid at the pharmacy is not part of that bill.

**Spread brand retail claim.** Hypothetical average wholesale price 100.00, guaranteed brand retail discount 20% and retail dispensing fee 1.00: the claim is billed at 80.00 plus 1.00, that is 81.00, whether the pharmacy was paid 75.00 or 85.00 for it.
